questions.question_text: The area enclosed by the curve $x=\sqrt{3}cos\theta,y=\sqrt{3}sin\theta$ is
questions.question_html: The area enclosed by the curve $x=\sqrt{3}cos\theta,y=\sqrt{3}sin\theta$ is

options.label: A
options.html: $\sqrt{3}\pi$ sq. units

options.label: B
options.html: $9\pi$ sq. units

options.label: C
options.html: $6\pi$ sq. units

options.label: D
options.html: $3\pi$ sq. units

questions.explanation_text: Given, $x=\sqrt{3}cos\theta,y=\sqrt{3}sin\theta$ We know the standard parametric form of a circle is $x=acos\theta,y=asin\theta$ This represents a circle with centre at the origin and radius $a$ . Here, $a=\sqrt{3}$ So the radius of the circle is $\sqrt{3}$ . Area enclosed by a circle is $\pi r^{2}$ So, $\text{Area}=\pi(\sqrt{3})^{2}$ $\text{Area}=3\pi$ Hence, the area enclosed by the curve is $3\pi\text{sq. units}$ Correct option: Option D.
questions.explanation_html:
Given,

$x=\sqrt{3}cos\theta,y=\sqrt{3}sin\theta$

We know the standard parametric form of a circle is

$x=acos\theta,y=asin\theta$

This represents a circle with centre at the origin and radius $a$ .

Here,

$a=\sqrt{3}$

So the radius of the circle is $\sqrt{3}$ .

Area enclosed by a circle is

$\pi r^{2}$

So,

$\text{Area}=\pi(\sqrt{3})^{2}$

$\text{Area}=3\pi$

Hence, the area enclosed by the curve is

$3\pi\text{sq. units}$

Correct option: Option D.

questions.question_text: If in two circles, arcs of the same length subtend angles $30^{\circ}$ and $78^{\circ}$ at the centre, then the ratio of their radii is
questions.question_html: If in two circles, arcs of the same length subtend angles $30^{\circ}$ and $78^{\circ}$ at the centre, then the ratio of their radii is
questions.explanation_text: Let the radii of the two circles be $r_{1}$ and $r_{2}$ . Let an arc of length $l$ subtend an angle of $30^{\circ}$ at the centre of the circle of radius $r_{1}$ , while let an arc of length $l$ subtend an angle of $78^{\circ}$ at the centre of the circle of radius $r_{2}$ . Now, $30^{\circ}=\frac{\pi}{6}$ radian and $78^{\circ}=\frac{13\pi}{30}$ radian We know that in a circle of radius $r$ unit, if an arc of length $l$ unit subtend an angle $\theta$ radian at the centre, then $\begin{aligned} & & \theta=\frac{l}{r}\text{or}l=r\theta \\ \therefore & & l=\frac{r_{1}\pi}{6}\text{and}l=\frac{r_{2}13\pi}{30} \\ \Rightarrow & & \frac{r_{1}\pi}{6}=\frac{r_{2}13\pi}{30} \\ \Rightarrow & & r_{1}=r_{2}\frac{13}{5} \\ \Rightarrow & & \frac{r_{1}}{r_{2}}=\frac{13}{5} \end{aligned}$

Now, $30^{\circ}=\frac{\pi}{6}$ radian and $78^{\circ}=\frac{13\pi}{30}$ radian

We know that in a circle of radius $r$ unit, if an arc of length $l$ unit subtend an angle $\theta$ radian at the centre, then

$\begin{aligned} & & \theta=\frac{l}{r}\text{or}l=r\theta \\ \therefore & & l=\frac{r_{1}\pi}{6}\text{and}l=\frac{r_{2}13\pi}{30} \\ \Rightarrow & & \frac{r_{1}\pi}{6}=\frac{r_{2}13\pi}{30} \\ \Rightarrow & & r_{1}=r_{2}\frac{13}{5} \\ \Rightarrow & & \frac{r_{1}}{r_{2}}=\frac{13}{5} \end{aligned}$

questions.question_text: The maximum area of a rectangle inscribed in the circle $(x+1)^{2}+(y-3)^{2}=64$ is
questions.question_html: The maximum area of a rectangle inscribed in the circle $(x+1)^{2}+(y-3)^{2}=64$ is

options.label: A
options.html: 64 sq units

options.label: B
options.html: 72 sq units

options.label: C
options.html: 128 sq units

options.label: D
options.html: 8 sq units

questions.explanation_text: To determine the maximum area of a rectangle inscribed in the circle given by the equation $(x+1)^{2}+(y-3)^{2}=64$ , we can use the known fact that for any rectangle inscribed in a circle, the maximum area is achieved when the rectangle is a square. This maximum area is given by the formula $2r^{2}$ , where $r$ is the radius of the circle. Looking at the provided circle equation: $(x+1)^{2}+(y-3)^{2}=64$ We can identify that the circle's center is at $(-1,3)$ and its radius is $\sqrt{64}=8$ . Therefore, the maximum area of a rectangle inscribed in this circle is: $2 \times (8)^{2}=2 \times 64=128\text{square units}$
questions.explanation_html:
To determine the maximum area of a rectangle inscribed in the circle given by the equation $(x+1)^{2}+(y-3)^{2}=64$ , we can use the known fact that for any rectangle inscribed in a circle, the maximum area is achieved when the rectangle is a square. This maximum area is given by the formula $2r^{2}$ , where $r$ is the radius of the circle.

Looking at the provided circle equation:

$(x+1)^{2}+(y-3)^{2}=64$

We can identify that the circle's center is at $(-1,3)$ and its radius is $\sqrt{64}=8$ .

Therefore, the maximum area of a rectangle inscribed in this circle is:

$2 \times (8)^{2}=2 \times 64=128\text{square units}$
